title: The Marshal of Marble Ranks
story: In the ruined moonlit amphitheatre, Stannivor drills an army of marble soldiers who march toward the sleeping village below. Mr 6 climbs the steps and offers a riddle instead of a fight — because he can see the ranks are perfectly arranged, and arrangements can be counted.
question: Stannivor's army stands in 12 rows of 15 marble soldiers. Mr 6's riddle turns 40% of them back into pigeons, and then a quarter of the soldiers who remain crumble into harmless gravel. How many marble soldiers are still standing?
solution: After 40% fly off as pigeons, 60% remain: 180 × 0.6 = 108.
A quarter of those crumble, so three quarters stay: 108 × 0.75 = 81 soldiers still standing.
praise: Multiplying the rows and columns first was exactly the right opening — the step left out was taking three quarters of what was LEFT, not of the whole army.
hint: Count the whole army first with rows × columns, then take each change in order — always applied to the number still standing.
victory: Eighty-one marble soldiers looked around, decided a maths-loving six was too clever to march against, and sat down to become very fine statues. The village woke up to a brand-new sculpture garden.
imagePrompt: Moonlit ruined amphitheatre where neat rows of marble soldiers stand frozen mid-march, pigeons bursting from their ranks, as a small caped knight-numeral 6 poses a riddle from the top step.
